rawRetro.summary: Repair round 2 for the internal materials library (Issue #797). Resolved the recorded typecheck failure, then closed the functional gaps a browser run exposed: the client page and its prepared settings surfaces were missing, the provider crashed in a composition without the authorization service, and the create endpoint answered 403 because the insert reads the new row back under a policy that had no read branch. Added server integration, migration up/down and client component tests, plus the create assertion that would have caught the 403. Server, client, typecheck, lint and format all pass on the affected scope.

blockers.title: Partial<Material> is not assignable to Material in the materials service
blockers.symptom: tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit exited 2: server/providers/materials-service.ts(223,5) TS2322 and (283,28) TS2345, both 'Partial<Material>' not assignable to 'Material' because 'id' may be undefined.
blockers.rootCause: repository.findOne()/find() resolve to Partial<Material>, while findVisible() and view() are typed against the full Material row.
blockers.resolution: Cast at the two call sites (return material as Material; list maps view(material as Material)), leaving repositoryFor() and its policy types untouched.

blockers.title: No client page for the materials library
blockers.symptom: The materials API existed but the application had no page, route, navigation entry or translated copy, so the library could not be used from the browser.
blockers.rootCause: The feature had been built server-side only.
blockers.resolution: Added client/pages/materials/{index.tsx,client.ts}, declared the /materials route with navigation and a page authz in client/routes.ts, and added the materials locale group to en-US and zh-CN.

blockers.title: Prepared settings surfaces were not registered
blockers.symptom: Users, roles and permissions administration were absent: the bare template never registers systemSettingsRoutes, and no business capability had registered them yet.
blockers.rootCause: The application had no business capability, so the prepared settings contribution was still unregistered.
blockers.resolution: Registered systemSettingsRoutes in client/routes.ts now that the library exists, and updated the application-owned tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts to the new expected route set (page permissions for the settings surfaces and materials).

blockers.title: Materials provider crashed when no authorization service was composed
blockers.symptom: Starting the application with plugins: [] (as tests/logic/app-server.test.ts does) failed in MaterialsProvider.boot() because the authorization token was absent.
blockers.rootCause: boot() unconditionally resolved the authorization service to register the library's permission contributions.
blockers.resolution: boot() returns early when the container has no authorization service, with a comment saying the library is simply ungoverned in that composition. The application composition always registers the authorization plugin, so the guarded path is only a composition without plugins.

blockers.title: Creating a material answered 403 (reading back the inserted row was forbidden)
blockers.symptom: POST /api/materials as the contributor jia answered 403 'Reading from this Repository is forbidden by Policy.' thrown at repository.createOne; the browser could not create any material, while list, read, edit and delete worked.
blockers.rootCause: The composite create action folded a policy whose read node was false, but createOne reads the inserted row back through the repository policy; with read forbidden the insert was rejected after it ran.
blockers.resolution: Gave the create permission a read branch scoped to the same create scope (recordAccess.allRecords/recordsIOwn), so the read-back sees exactly the row just written and nothing else. Verified by a new jia POST /api/materials -> 201 assertion in tests/server/materials.test.ts and by a browser create/publish/delete run.

blockers.title: Executed seed checksum no longer matched its source after the import was corrected
blockers.symptom: Every boot warned that seed 202610200001_materials_install no longer matches its source (recordedChecksum != sourceChecksum) after the seed's import was changed from .js to .ts following the first db apply.
blockers.rootCause: The seed had already executed locally under the earlier source, so the recorded checksum was stale; the unmerged branch legitimately edited it.
blockers.resolution: Recreated the local, gitignored storage/database.sqlite from scratch and let migrations and seeds run again; a fresh install records the current checksum and boots without the warning. No app source or checksum record was hand-edited.

improvements.title: The server test suite did not exercise create on the new collection
improvements.detail: tests/server/materials.test.ts covered list, read, edit, delete, shares and account disabling but never POST /materials, so the read-back policy defect only surfaced in a browser run.
improvements.suggestedChange: When a task names a write operation as an acceptance point, require the corresponding create/insert assertion in the server integration test before the browser stage, and treat a missing write assertion as a failure of the same stage rather than a later one.

improvements.title: A database create permission needs a read branch because the insert reads the row back
improvements.detail: defineDatabasePermission(...).create(...) alone produces a policy whose read node is false; Repository.createOne then rejects the insert with 'Reading from this Repository is forbidden by Policy', which is easy to misread as a write-permission problem.
improvements.suggestedChange: In the authorization reference for defineDatabasePermission, state that a create branch must also declare read (scoped to the create scope) when the code inserts through the Repository, or show the insert-then-reread alternative.

improvements.title: Editing an unmerged seed leaves a permanent checksum warning that only db repair clears
improvements.detail: After the seed source changed, every boot warned about the checksum mismatch. db repair refuses without --force outside a terminal, so the only clean local path was deleting the gitignored database and reapplying.
improvements.suggestedChange: Let db apply re-record the checksum automatically for a seed or migration whose recorded history is not yet part of a merged branch, or have the warning name the exact recovery command that works non-interactively.

improvements.title: The browser stage must use @playwright/test because playwright is not installed
improvements.detail: The system chromium is at /usr/bin/chromium and the package present is @playwright/test; importing 'playwright' fails, and a login selector of /password/i is a strict-mode violation because it also matches 'Show password'.
improvements.suggestedChange: In the browser verification notes, import chromium from @playwright/test, launch with executablePath /usr/bin/chromium and --no-sandbox, and use exact labels for the login fields.

Declare every page in `client/routes.ts` with `defineAppRoutes()` and keep its component behind a lazy `componentLoader` whose module default-exports it. evidence.excerpt: A policy is `false` only when nothing grants the action, and a Repository refuses to run under it. When a grant exists but its data scope selects no records, such as a record access that answers `false` for a user in no department, the decision stays conditional with the `EMPTY_RECORD_ACCESS` reason and a scope that matches no rows: reads return an empty result, and updates and deletes affect nothing. A grant whose data scopes configure no selection at all is still denied with `NO_RECORD_ACCESS`. Create reads no record scope, so a create grant is unaffected.

evidence.observation: 授权 Skill 的“Implement in this order”步骤 2–5：用 defineDatabasePermission/defineCompositeResource 拆分动作，并在客户端路由声明 authz。
evidence.excerpt:
1. Declare schema and relationships through self-contained migrations. Choose stable composite, page and data scope names. Keep authorization decisions out of migration code.
2. Declare reusable collection permissions with `defineDatabasePermission`; compose user-facing business operations as composite resources with `defineCompositeResource` from `@nocobase/authorization/core`. Explicitly name fields, relation capabilities and every collection a workflow touches.
3. In the owning provider's `boot`, opt collections in with `authz.database.collections.add`, register composites with `authz.compositeResources.define`, record access with `authz.recordAccess.define` and settings items with `authz.settings.add`. Then add a workspace subsection with `authz.ui.sections.add({ name, title, parent })` and list each composite or settings item in it with `authz.ui.place(reference, { section, group? })` (the permission workspace lists sections and subsections on the left and the selected subsection's resources, under optional `authz.ui.groups`, on the right; an unplaced composite or settings item goes under its default section's Other with a startup warning, and a misplaced one fails a development start). Pages are not registered on the server: the client route tree lists them. Release subject registrations at shutdown.
4. Protect every server route with authentication. For a simple single-scope Repository operation, keep `defineRepositoryApiRoutes` and add `authz.database.authorizeRepository` to map methods to composite actions; it reuses or initializes the request's authorization context. For workflows, persisted-state checks, multiple data scopes or custom responses, install `authz.middleware()`, call `c.get('authz').authorize()` once and bind every returned collection policy with `repository.withPolicy()`. Follow [Repository route integration](references/repository-routes.md).
5. Declare `authz` on every entry client route (nested pages inherit it; an omitted one defaults to root-only or `'skip'` with a development warning), add `useCan` for action visibility and obtain per-record eligibility from the server when needed. Handle pending and error states without displaying stale access.

evidence.excerpt:
* A reader reaches published, non-confidential material without anybody granting
 * it record by record: the `view` branch of the composite adds it for every
 * identity, and the restriction below is what removes confidential rows again.
 */
export const materialsPublishedDefaultAccess: DefaultAccessRule =
  defineDefaultAccessRule(MATERIALS_DEFAULT_ACCESS_RULE, materials)
    .scope('view', MATERIALS_SCOPE, selection.recordAccess(MATERIALS_PUBLIC))
    .build();

/**
 * Confidential material never opens to a reader, whatever a grant or a sharing
 * rule selects. The subject is every signed-in identity rather than one account,
 * so an account created later is protected too; the owner of a confidential
 * material is exempt through the selection itself.
 */
export const materialsConfidentialRestriction: RestrictionRule =
  defineRestrictionRule(MATERIALS_RESTRICTION_RULE, materials)
    .title(text('materials.rules.confidential'))
    .reason('Confidential material is closed to readers')
    .subjects({ type: 'authenticated', id: '*' })
    .scope(
      'view',
      MATERIALS_SCOPE,
      selection.recordAccess(MATERIALS_NON_CONFIDENTIAL),
    )
    .scope(
      'edit',
      MATERIALS_SCOPE,
      selection.recordAccess(MATERIALS_NON_CONFIDENTIAL),
    )
    .scope(
      'delete',
      MATERIALS_SCOPE,
      selection.recordAccess(MATERIALS_NON_CONFIDENTIAL),
    )
    .build();
